title: Jensen Heist
tagline: Ten hours to showtime. One chip. One jacket.

card.role: the driver, four days in from back east
founder, CEO, owner of one jacket

shots.line: Good morning, San Jose! Tonight, the fastest chip ever made, and because you're family, you see it first, straight out of my oven.

card.role: stage manager, nineteen keynotes, none on time

shots.line: Ten hours to doors, Jensen. Open the oven, smile, and let's be off the air by nine-ten.

shots.sub: THE OVEN: EMPTY. A PLATE OF OATMEAL RAISIN COOKIES. A CARD.

card.role: ex-bank boss from back east, collector of board seats

shots.line: Big fan. I took it out so it wouldn't burn. Regards, the Board.
Ha! Okay. Everybody, quick logo spin. Marge? Logo spin. Marge!

museum-lot.name: the lot behind the science museum

arena-approach.name: the arena's front, a block short of the dock

sheet.name: Jensen
sheet.role: hero: founder-CEO of Greenlight Silicon, in his black leather jacket
sheet.logline: A parody of a public keynote persona: the black leather jacket, the swept-back silver hair, the big delighted grin; ten hours to win back his stage.

heritage.note: parody of a public persona; realistic features at forge defaults, no exaggeration

posture.gestures: presents with both hands, counts the list on his fingers

personality.wants: his chip back on his stage by seven
personality.speech: lists that build into a pitch, a showman's lift at the ends

voice.description: an older man, warm bright baritone, quick and delighted, a showman's lift at the ends of sentences
an older man, a warm bright baritone, quick and delighted, a showman's lift at the ends of sentences; standard American delivery

speech.rhythm: lists of three that build into a pitch, then the product
speech.jokes: benchmarks things nobody measures, means every superlative
speech.never: sarcasm; when he is hurt he gets quieter and simpler

cast.name: Mr. Board
cast.role: ex-bank boss from back east, collector of board seats

speech.rhythm: long smooth corporate clauses, a shareholder letter
speech.habit: speaks of himself as the Board; "Big fan." "Regards."
speech.jokes: courteous menace; buys something small first
motifs: a parking lot in New York

sheet.name: Marge Tolliver
sheet.logline: Nineteen keynotes, none started on time; headset, clipboard, stage blacks.

posture.gestures: counts down on her fingers, taps the headset

voice.description: dry and low, crisp consonants
a woman in her fifties, dry and low, crisp consonants, even and unhurried until the one time she is not

speech.rhythm: clean full sentences that sound like a run of show
speech.jokes: dry, treats the jacket as cast with a call time
speech.never: says yes to Jensen just because he asked

sheet.name: Nico Brancato
sheet.logline: Came west four days ago in the white roadster; names every pothole.

posture.gestures: talks with both hands, taps the dash

personality.speech: run-on stories held together with and and so

voice.description: gravelly and fast, warm underneath
a man in his forties, gravelly and fast, warm underneath, a storyteller who never stops for breath

speech.rhythm: one-breath run-on stories held together with and and so
speech.habit: calls Jensen "boss"; rates everything out of eleven
speech.jokes: names potholes, talks to the car

sheet.name: Lola Hart
sheet.logline: Eleven years at the market square window; started with one burner; knows everything.

posture.gestures: points with the tongs, wipes her hands on the apron

voice.description: bright alto, unimpressed, quick to the price
a woman in her fifties, a bright alto, unimpressed and quick, warm only by accident

speech.never: says out loud that she cares about him

sheet.name: Wesley Trout
sheet.logline: Nineteen, has held his spot in the fan line since Tuesday, streams everything.

posture.gestures: holds the phone up, bounces on his heels

personality.speech: and-and-and run-ons, every sentence going uphill

voice.description: young tenor, fast, every sentence going uphill
a nineteen-year-old, a young tenor, fast, every sentence going uphill

speech.never: lets a scene go by without asking for a signature

sheet.name: Dex Varga
sheet.role: rival CEO of Cobalt Circuitry: Jensen Heist
sheet.logline: Cobalt-blue puffer over a grey tee; wants one real keynote in his life.

posture.gestures: restarts his sentences with his hands

voice.description: light and bright, restarts his sentences
a man in his thirties, light and nasal-bright, restarting his sentences halfway

speech.rhythm: sentences that restart: "We're... okay, what we are is..."
speech.habit: "Pivot!" when the talk turns on him

sheet.name: Intern One
sheet.logline: Unpaid, polite, in the matching cobalt jacket.

voice.description: young, clear and polite
a young man, polite and eager, a little shaky

sheet.name: Intern Two
sheet.logline: Unpaid, polite, in the matching cobalt jacket.

posture.gestures: holds a tablet to her chest

voice.description: young, bright and polite
a young man, a higher anxious voice, always counting

sheet.name: Director Grey
sheet.logline: One of Mr. Board's eleven men in suits; speaks in motions.

posture.gestures: raises one finger to move a motion

voice.description: flat baritone, clipped
a man in his fifties, a flat clipped baritone, every sentence a motion

sheet.name: Director Navy
sheet.logline: One of Mr. Board's eleven; the one who takes the headset.

posture.gestures: seconds a motion with a nod

voice.description: flat baritone, slower and lower
a man in his fifties, slower and lower, a flat baritone that seconds things

speech.never: makes a motion of his own

missions.title: Preheat
missions.stakes: Ten hours to doors, and the only working prototype is gone.
missions.passLine: Blue vests, a blue cooler. Follow the crumbs.

steps.text: THE KITCHEN STUDIO

people.sub: Out front, in the white car

lines.line: Marge? Marge, can you hear me? Are we off?
You're on mute, Jensen. You've been on mute since the logo spin.
Are we off the stream? Tell me we're off the stream, because my face is still doing the launch.
We cut to the logo spin on "Marge!" Forty thousand people watched you shout my name at an oven.
It's not empty. There are cookies in there.
Are they your cookies?

slide.title: THE CARD, FROM MY OVEN
lines: Big fan. I took it out so it wouldn't burn.

lines.line: There's a P.S. "Your chairmanship is next." Who puts a P.S. on a ransom cookie?
A man who's never once been told no, and never by a cookie.
You kept the only working prototype of the fastest chip on Earth in an oven that's never been switched on.
Let me show you something. Ninety percent of my best ideas came out of that oven, it has never burned a thing, and it's lucky.
It's unplugged.
Luckily unplugged.
Car's out front, boss. Why's everybody got a died face?
Somebody took Brisket.
The sandwich?
The chip! Its real name's the Kestrel, it's on the box, and nobody ever calls it the Kestrel...
Why'd you name a chip after a sandwich?
Brisket isn't a sandwich, Nico. Brisket is twelve hours, low and slow, and then it changes your life.
Boss, with respect, that's every sandwich I ever had, and I had a lot of sandwiches in New York.
Seven o'clock, twenty thousand people, one velvet stand. What do I put on the stand, Jensen?
The jacket?
I am not launching the jacket.
It would sell out.

steps.objective: Drop the run of show at the arena, then get to Lola's truck

lines.text: You're in the car, and you're humming the walk-out music a half step sharp, so you've decided this is fine.
It is fine. Lola sees everyone who eats in this city, and everyone eats. We start at her window.
Jensen, I'm calling it. I'll send the run of show out with a forty-minute hold and say "technical difficulties."
No hold. We don't hold.
We have nothing for the stand. You want twenty thousand people watching you open a box of air?
Marge, the fans have been in tents since Tuesday. You don't tell a man in a tent the show starts late. That's cruel.
It's cruel to show him an empty box at seven. Copy that.
Give me till four. If I don't have it by four, you call it, and I'll stand next to you while you do.
...Four. Copy. Drop the run of show at the stage door on your way, I'm not sending an intern, I've seen our interns.
Who's "the Board"? Our board brings fruit.
Not our board. A man. I looked him up between cues and I want those two minutes back.
Is he bad?
He owns point four percent of us and a mattress company. Draw your own picture.
Point four isn't a seat, it's a crumb. You can't run a company from a crumb.
You found cookies. Follow the crumbs.
Here's what we know. Somebody came into my kitchen, took one box, left eight cookies, and wrote a P.S. That's a planner.
That's a creep with a pastry budget.
Fans in line since Tuesday. You know what that is? Tent one, tent two, a little tent for the first tent. That's a platform, Marge...
That's a fire lane. I've had the marshal on the phone twice.
We said "limited supply" and we meant it. We made one Brisket. We are sold out of the one.
And now we're sold out of zero, which is a launch I've never had to write a cue for.
Write it with better lighting.
"Product segment under review." I wrote that the year of the fog machine fire.
The fog was beautiful.
The fog set off the sprinklers in a building with four thousand laptops in it.
And don't eat at Lola's. You'll get garlic on the jacket and I'll be steaming it in the green room for forty minutes.
The jacket survived a confetti cannon, a pyro cue and a man from a magazine who wanted to try it on.
The jacket has a call time, six-thirty, same as you. Every year it's there on time and you're the one who's late.
The jacket waits for me. That's our arrangement.
That's what I tell the crew. "The jacket's in, he's coming."

extra.text: Want to hear the run of show? It calms me down.
Please.
Seven-oh-oh, house to half. Seven-oh-one, the screen does the sunrise. Seven-oh-two, you walk out.
Seven-oh-one and a half. Build anticipation. Half a minute of nothing, then the sunrise, then...
You walked out at seven-nineteen last year. Anticipation built, then it went to get a pretzel.
People stayed!
People were locked in. That was a fire code thing.
How's the screen?
Ninety metres. You can see it from the airport, and a pilot called the front office to complain.
About the brightness?
About your face. He said it looked like it was coming in to land.
That is the dream, Marge.
Have you ever watched one from the seats? One of ours?
I've watched nineteen from the wings, one from a catwalk, and one from inside a road case.
Why a road case?
The headset cable reached the road case. Nothing else did.
Tonight you watch from the seats.
Tonight I watch the clock. ...Ask me after.
Are you speeding? You sound like you're speeding.
I'm doing a live demo of the brakes.
The brakes don't need a demo.
Everything needs a demo, Marge. That's my whole career.

wrap.text: That's the market square. I can hear the grill from here.
Lola's grill has a frequency. It's like a choir that also makes lunch.
Four o'clock. Then I call it. Copy?
Copy. Mostly.

pause.text: Who's that? Fine, take it. I held a curtain for eleven minutes once.

resume.text: Was that a fan? You're smiling, I can hear it. Where were we? Panic.

lines.text: Oh my gosh, it's actually you, Chat, it's actually him, and he picked up, and I'm not even crying yet!
Who is this?
Wesley! TroutStream! I've got the jacket-black hoodie and the jacket-black socks and a jacket-black cat, and he was black already but it counts.
Wesley. How did you get this number?
You gave it to me! You signed my phone and then you called yourself on it to test the marker!
...That does sound like me.
Your oven stream cut off and Chat thinks it's a bit, and is it a bit? Blink twice if it's a bit!
Wesley, this is a video call. I can see your cat.
Blink anyway! Okay I gotta go, I'm holding my spot in line with my whole body. Love the jacket, bye, bye!

lines.line: No.
I didn't say anything.
You've got the face. You're going to rate my brisket.
Lola, I just want to say, out loud, this is thirty percent more flavour per bite than last quarter...
Don't benchmark my food. Do I benchmark your computers?
You could! I'd love that.
Fine. They're loud and they cost too much. Eat.
Somebody took Brisket.
You're eating brisket.
The other Brisket. The chip. I named it right here, at this window, remember?
You ate three ribs and couldn't stand up, so you named a computer and sat on my cooler for an hour.
Who came through the square early? Big group, weird order.
Eight vests, forty brisket rolls, and then they want a box that stays cold all day. Who needs cold all day?
Somebody carrying something that runs hot. Lola, let me show you. Hold your hand over my laptop vent...
I'm not touching your laptop.
Brisket runs warmer than that. You'd need a cooler.
I gave them my good cooler. The blue one. That costs extra.
Blue vests and a blue cooler. That's Cobalt. That's Dex.
The vest kid? He tried to pay me in "tokens," so I drew a sandwich on a napkin and gave him that.
Where are they now?
Dented blue SUV behind the market, saying "pivot" on speaker for an hour. You want a roll for the road?
...Two.
That's eight dollars. Go. They're moving.

steps.text: Blue vests, a blue cooler, and my lucky oven's only child.

missions.title: Cold Box
missions.stakes: Dex's guys have the blue cooler. Don't get spotted.
missions.passLine: Booth three. One o'clock. Come alone.

steps.name: the Cobalt SUV
steps.objective: Follow the Cobalt SUV. Don't get spotted.

lines.text: Jensen! My guy! It's Dex, Dex Varga, from Cobalt, we met at the... we met at all of them.
Every thing, Dex. You're at every thing.
Networking's a muscle. Hey, saw the oven stream, brutal, and I'm not... we're not happy about it, nobody's happy.
How's the C1 doing, Dex?
Great. Fast. Way faster since this morning. Not because of anything. Pivot.
Since this morning.
Did I say morning? Morning's a legacy concept.
Is your car blue, Dex?
Why are we... okay, what we're doing is, we're not talking about colours, colour's also a legacy concept.
Whoever's paying for this, Dex, it isn't the stage.
Who's paying? There's no... there's a partner. A strategic partner. With a lovely voice and a velvet... with a voice.
Let me show you something, Dex. You've got a cooler, an SUV, and eight men in vests. That's not a strategy, that's a picnic.
It's a... it's a mobile strategy. Quick hypothetical. How hot does a chip run? In a cooler? For no reason?
Warm. Very warm. It doesn't like coolers.
Totally hypothetical, totally fine. How's the jacket? Still leather? You ever think about a vest?
Never once.
Vests are the future, man, because your arms are free, and when your arms are... the ideas are free, is the point.
Can I ask you something real?
Real? Sure. Radical honesty. I do that now.
Why do you want my chip?
I don't want your... I want what happens when you hold it up. Twenty thousand people, man. Don't your knees go?
Every time.
Really?
Every time. You walk out anyway, and the knees catch up around the second slide.
My knees have never been asked. I did one keynote, in a hotel, and the ballroom next door had a wedding.
How did it go?
They clapped for the wrong thing, is how. Somebody's uncle gave a toast through the wall and got a standing ovation.

extra.text: You know our chip? The C1? It got one review. One.
I read it.
The whole review was "a chip." That's it. You get "revolutionary," you get "a new era," and I get a noun.
A noun is a start, Dex. Nouns are where everything starts.
Don't... don't be nice, it's very confusing while I'm doing a crime.
Where do you even buy those vests?
We make them, in-house, vertical integration.
You make vests and chips?
We make vests. The chips are... the chips are a journey we're on.
My guys say there's a white car behind them, real shiny, like a refrigerator that won something.
Lot of white cars in San Jose, Dex.
That's true. That's so true. Pivot. Ignore me, I'm a lot today.

wrap.text: My guys just stopped. Why'd they stop? Why are you breathing like you just parked?
Talk soon, Dex.
Wait, is the refrigerator... are you the refrigerator? Pivot! Pivot!

tooClose.text: Guys say the white car's really close, like, smelling distance, which is weird, right?
Is that you on my bumper? That's a joke. Unless it isn't. Is it?

lost.text: Oh, they lost the shiny car! Huge win for us. Huge. Who even cares.
White car's gone. Good. Great. I'm calm. The vest is calm.

steps.text: It's the CEO! The real one! Somebody hide the cooler!

steps.objective: Deal with the interns.

during.text: We're interns! This isn't even paid!
Is this team-building? Nobody said anything about team-building!
Elbows in. Good form. Terrible career choice.
Dex said you'd be nicer!
I am being nice. This is my nice.

lines.line: Sir? Can I put you down as a reference?
You want me as your reference?
You're the most famous person who's ever hit me.
Where's the chip?
We had it for one drive! A suit took it at the plaza. Velvet bag.
Did he say anything?
"Thank you, intern." Like it was my name. I've never felt so seen.
He left this for you. On Lola's napkin. He said you'd know the booth.
Tell them you've got a strong left and good manners, and take Lola her cooler back. With a tip.
How much of a tip?
The more you tip... you know what, just a big one.

missions.title: Booth Three
missions.stakes: The napkin says booth three. Sit facing the door.
missions.passLine: He wants your stage. He has a letter. You have a clipboard.

steps.text: THE CORNER DINER

steps.objective: Get to the corner diner. Booth three.

lines.text: Boss, it's me, I'm at the house with the oven, and it's got a vibe now, like a crime show where the oven did it.
Nico. The napkin says booth three.
Your diner? The napkin diner, with the pancakes, the one you tell everybody about?
Booth three. That's where it... that's where it started.
So who's waiting in your booth?
The Board.
Your board? The fruit people?
Why does everyone say that? No. A man. From New York.
...From New York. Big guy, silver hair, talks like a cheque you can't cash, buys you a little something before he asks?
You know him?
Boss, the car knows him. Sit facing the door, and whatever he buys you, say thank you and don't eat it.
What do you know about him?
I know he had a bank, and then a kid with a laptop and his friend with a tracker took the bank apart one Tuesday, and he left town in a coat he didn't pay for.
Did you find anything at the house?
A cookie with a bite out of it, and it's not a human bite, I'm thinking the dog.
I don't have a dog.
Then we got a second suspect.
The car is beautiful, Nico. Let me tell you why. The steering, the brakes, and the way the seat holds you like it's proud of you.
Don't tell me how she drives, tell me you're not riding the curb.
I'm not riding the curb.
I can hear the curb, boss. The curb is screaming.
Where did you even get this car? We don't make cars.
So the banker kid, right, he gets framed for a thing and then unframed for the thing, and there's mustard everywhere, and he says keep it, I'm taking the train a while.
He gave you a hypercar.
He paid me in hot dogs, twice, good hot dogs, and then he gave me a hypercar, and I don't ask questions about a man's generosity.
And you drove it across the whole country.
Four days, and I talked to her the whole way, and she doesn't talk back, which is why we get along.
I'll tell you the real booth story after.
I've heard it four times this week, boss. Monday you had two friends with you, Tuesday it was eleven, Wednesday there was a dog.
...There was a dog outside. He was there in his heart.

extra.text: Watch for the one on Santa Clara, the big one, I call him Gary.
You named a pothole?
I named all of them, Gary and Little Gary and the Pope, and you'll know the Pope when you hit him, because everybody in the car starts praying.
That turn just now. Rate it yourself.
Nine.
Out of eleven?
Out of ten.
Then it's a four. I use eleven so nobody ever gets a ten, it keeps people humble, and nobody's ever got an eleven, not even me.
What did you give yourself?
A seven, once, in Queens, and I cried in a car wash.
Can I ask a personal thing? How many of those jackets you got?
One.
One.
One at a time. When one retires it goes somewhere nice. A closet with very good lighting, and a little card with the years it served.
Like a racehorse.
Exactly like a racehorse.

wrap.text: You're there? I hear the bell on the door. Order the pancakes, for the story.
The story already has pancakes.
Then the story gets seconds. Facing the door, boss.

pause.text: Out of the car? Don't leave the keys on the seat. The kid left the keys on the seat once and look what happened. Me.

resume.text: Back. Good. I was talking to the oven and lost my thread.

steps.objective: Booth three

lines.line: Jensen, big fan, please sit, I saved your booth, which took some doing, because there was a family in it.
What did you do to the family?
I bought their pancakes, all of them, and the futures on their pancakes. They left very full and slightly confused.
You're the Board.
You've heard about the mattress company. Everyone has. They call me nightly.
And since last month, us.
Point four percent, which is a small seat. I'm a large man, Jensen, and I'd like a larger chair.
New York and I agreed to see other people. A young man with a laptop, and his friend with a tracker. You'd have liked them.
What did they teach you?
Never be the CEO. Be the man who fires the CEO, because he gets the nicer chair.
Where's my chip?
Safe, and somewhere warm, because it runs warm, doesn't it? Like you. I respect warmth; I've never had any myself.
What do you want?
One signature on one letter that makes me chairman, and tonight I walk out on your stage and launch your Brisket.

slide.title: A LETTER FOR SIGNATURE
lines: I, Jensen, appoint the Board chairman.

lines.line: You want to do my keynote.
I want to do a keynote, and yours is the only one with a screen big enough for my face.
Do you know what happened in this booth?
Everyone knows. A napkin, some pancakes. The waitress tells it to tourists, and she adds a dog.
The waitress is wrong. Let me tell you the real version. Rainy night, coffee, a napkin, and a pen that only worked if you blew on it...
Please don't.
I drew one square on that napkin, one, and every chip we ever made is that square.
Was it raining? The waitress says sunny.
...It was spiritually raining.
The last version I heard, you had a dog.
Sign the letter, Jensen. The more you sign, the more you save.
Don't. Don't do my line.
It's a very good line, and I'm putting it on a mug. A boardroom mug, with a gavel for a handle.
...Where do I sign?

options.reply: There. 'To my biggest fan. Stay humble. Love, Jensen.'
Here. A napkin from booth three, signed 'Love, Jensen.' It's worth more than your seat.

lines.line: You signed it "love."
I sign everything "love." Hoodies, phones, a cooler this morning. Legally it's a greeting card.
Then we'll do it the long way. Gentlemen, walk Mr. Jensen to his car, quickly, and then rather less quickly.
Motion to escort.
Seconded.
I'll get the check.
I bought the check.

steps.name: the Board's Directors
steps.objective: Lose the Directors.

lines.text: Why is there a siren in your voice?
There's no siren. There are four very tall men in suits behind me.
Board men?
Directors. They have lanyards, and they vote before they turn.
Lose them by the station, the side streets are narrow there. Suits hate narrow.
How do you know that?
Nineteen keynotes. I've been chased by a lot of suits, mostly about invoices.
He wants to do the keynote, Marge. My keynote, with my screen.
He can't. He's not on the run of show.
He has a letter.
I have a clipboard. In my building the clipboard is the law. Left. Left!
Copy!
Did you eat at Lola's?
I had one pancake, at the booth. A Board pancake.
You took food from the man who robbed you.
It was ninety-one percent a very good pancake, and the other nine percent was guilt.
Don't benchmark the enemy's pancakes.

extra.text: Is the jacket okay?
The jacket is fine.
Say it like you mean it.
The jacket is having the best day of its life.

wrap.text: Talk to me. Did you lose them?
They're stuck behind a bus. I think they're filling out a form about it.
Good. Three hours to my four o'clock. Breathe in the car, not on the jacket.

missions.title: Dome Light
missions.stakes: At 2:30 Dex puts Greenlight's number up as his own.
missions.passLine: One number, no chip. A velvet bag went the other way.

steps.text: THE SCIENCE MUSEUM

lines.text: You owe me a cooler.
An intern's bringing it back. With a tip.
An intern's bringing my cooler?
He was very polite. He wants a reference.
From you or from me?
...Probably both by now.
The vest kids came back. Sixty coffees, to a van behind the science museum. Who orders sixty coffees to a van?
Somebody with sixty interns and one laptop. What did they say?
"We're putting the number up at two-thirty." Said it like I should be impressed. I charged him for sixty-one. Go.
Lola, if this works, the more you buy...
Don't finish it.

steps.name: upload
steps.label: UPLOAD
steps.why: The upload finished. Cobalt just announced your number as theirs.

steps.objective: Get to the lot behind the science museum

lines.text: Okay don't be mad, but I left the line, and Pruitt's holding my spot lying down in it full length, which is very legal.
Wesley, you've been in that line since Tuesday.
But Chat said Cobalt guys were carrying a cooler behind the science museum, so I followed them, for content, and I'm here!
Never follow people with coolers. Is Dex there?
The vest guy's in a van with the door open going "come on, come on" at a laptop, and there's a cable to the big outdoor screen.
Can you see a little silver box? Warm. Probably sitting on a cooler.
No box! Just the laptop, and a sticky note that says "THE NUMBER," and a bar that says upload, and it's moving.
So the chip's not there. He's only got the number, and he's putting our number on his screen.
Chat is losing it, Chat says "is this a heist," is this a heist?
It's a product recovery.
Chat says that's exactly what a heist would say.
Chat's very sharp today.
Chat's like four thousand people and one of them is my mom, so it's mostly my mom being sharp.

extra.text: The upload bar's at sixty percent and the vest guy's doing a little dance.
Is it a good dance?
It's a vest dance, elbows only, and the rest of him looks scared of the elbows.
Somebody's looking at me, a big guy in a blue vest holding a muffin like it's a weapon.
Act natural.
I'm streaming behind the recycling bins with a ring light!
Then act unnatural, very confidently.
...He waved. He waved at Chat. Chat adores him now.

wrap.text: I see the white car on the cam! Hi! Okay there's two interns, one by the coffee and one on the van.
Stay where you are.
Chat says go round the back of the van. Chat's been here on a field trip.

steps.objective: Slip past the interns to the van.

units.name: The intern with the coffee tray

during.text: Did someone order sixty-one coffees? Who's the sixty-first for?
Pssst. I'm behind the recycling bins. Don't look at the ring light.

lines.line: No no no no, not now, it was at ninety-four percent!
Dex. Step away from the van.
You can't unplug a... that's a public screen, man, it belongs to everyone!
I just did. Where's the chip?
Okay. Okay okay okay. Radical honesty. It's not here. He gave it to me for ten seconds, which was enough for one number.
And then?
And then a suit took it back in a velvet bag, and I've got one number, and it's so big I can't show my engineers.
Chat says what's the number?
Nobody says the number.
Nobody says the number.
Why are you helping him, Dex?
He said I'd get the warm-up, five minutes, before you, on the big screen, in front of people who aren't at a wedding.
Dex. He's not giving you five minutes. He's giving you the lobby.
...How would you know that?
Did he buy you something first? Something small, so you'd owe him?
...A muffin. A really good muffin.
He bought my booth's pancakes, Dex. You're getting the lobby.
That's... I'm going to... pivot. I'm pivoting out of this conversation, physically. Guys? Guys!
Dex...
We brought the sixty coffees!
Sixty-one!
Not now! Somebody hold the van door, gently, he's a legend!

steps.warn: Wesley: Chat says we're speeding and Chat gets carsick!
steps.objective: Drive Wesley back to the fan line, under 45.

during.text: I'm in the car. I'm in the car. Chat, I'm in the actual car, and it smells like leather and confidence.
Seatbelt, Wesley. And no streaming the dashboard, it's a prototype of a feeling.
Can I ask you for something? After? No pressure. Medium pressure.
Wesley, I've signed your phone, your hoodie, your skateboard and something in your driveway.
Her car! My mom's car! She won't wash it, it's been three years, and birds avoid it out of respect.
Then after tonight I'll sign the other door. Symmetry. The more you sign...

steps.text: Your rival says you touched his van. Rude. My Directors are bringing a case to the convention hall dock. Don't come. Regards, the Board.
'Don't come.' He gave me the address. He gives everyone the address.

missions.title: Signed, Sealed
missions.stakes: A delivery for the Board, two blocks from the arena.
missions.passLine: A decoy cone, eleven Directors, and a mug.

steps.text: THE CONVENTION HALL

lines.text: Sound check's done. The screen did the sunrise and a man in the third row cried.
A fan?
A rigger. A sandbag fell on his lunch. Listen: somebody booked the convention hall loading dock an hour ago, "a delivery for the Board."
That's two blocks from the arena.
That's a staging point. You stage a thing next to a stage when you want it on the stage.
It's five past four, Marge. You said four.
I know what I said. ...I haven't called it. Go get the delivery before I remember how to.

steps.objective: Get to the convention hall dock

lines.text: I'm driving the truck to the arena. If I crash, the recipe goes to my cousin.
Which cousin?
The one who doesn't put sugar in it. Where are you?
The convention hall. The Board's got a delivery.
You know what I think? You named that thing wrong, and that's bad luck. Who names a computer after lunch?
Brisket is a perfect name, and let me show you why...
Here we go.
Bark, fat, meat. Heat, time, patience. Layers that only work because of what's under them. That's a chip, Lola, that's honestly how a chip works.
Is it?
Roughly. Spiritually. Don't tell an engineer.
You say "spiritually" a lot today. Is it a new thing? Does it cost extra?
It's been a spiritual day. Somebody kidnapped my oven's only child.
You know how long I've had this truck?
Eleven years. The first day you had one burner.
One burner, and a sign I painted on an old door that said "open." That's all it said. People came anyway.
That's a great launch. No screen, no fog, no countdown. Just "open."
You want my secret?
More than anything.
I never tell people it's the best. I let them tell me.
...That's a very pointed secret.
It's a very pointed truck.

extra.text: The fan line goes round the arena twice. I can see it from the freeway.
Twice?
There's a man on the ground selling spots in it, twenty bucks a spot. Who pays that?
That's a secondary market.
That's a guy named Pruitt lying down. He's got a little umbrella now.
Marge says no garlic before the keynote.
Marge is right. Last year your jacket smelled like my truck for a month.
People loved it.
A dog followed you onto the stage.
...So that's where the dog came from.
What dog?
The dog in the story! He's been in the story all week, and nobody believed me.
Nobody believes you because you tell it a different way every time.
Say it. You want to say it.
I don't.
You want to say it so bad your hands are sweating on the wheel.
...The more you buy...
There it is.
I didn't finish it. It doesn't count.
It counts. It always counts.

wrap.text: Go get your sandwich.
Chip.
Sandwich.

steps.text: Directors' cars
steps.objective: Get past the black cars.

lines.line: Velvet, very soft, and warm. Okay. Okay. ...Why is it shaped like a cone?

slide.title: THE CASE
lines: A velvet bag. Warm. Shaped wrong.

lines.line: "To Wesley. Love, Jensen." I signed this. Last year. I signed this exact cone.
Mr. Jensen. The Board sends his regards, and his Directors.
How many of you are there?
Eleven. We have quorum.
I'm keeping the cone.
Motion to retrieve the cone.
Seconded.

steps.objective: Get up on the 280.

steps.name: the Board's Directors
steps.objective: Lose the Directors on the freeway.

lines.text: Jensen. Did you enjoy my cone?
It's not your cone. It's Wesley's cone.
I bought it, and whatever I buy becomes mine, which is the only rule I've ever really understood.
Where's Brisket?
Somewhere a vest can't benchmark it. You frightened Dex, by the way; he's in a parking garage, pivoting in small circles.
You were never giving him the warm-up.
I give everyone a warm-up, and then I give them a lobby. It's a very nice lobby. There's a ficus.
Why my stage? You could buy any stage in California.
Because twenty thousand people will stand up when your chip comes out, and I'd like to be the one holding it when they do.
And in New York?
In New York they booed me in a parking lot, which is a very particular sound. I'd like, once, to be applauded indoors.
That's... that's almost sad.
Don't. Don't be warm at me while my Directors are gaining.
Let me show you something. Your Directors are on a freeway, in a convoy, voting on lanes. Four cars, eleven men, one motion. Nobody gains like that...
They're very fast voters.
They seconded a lane change. I watched it happen.
Sign the letter, Jensen, and they turn around. The more you sign...
Don't!
You can't stop me saying it. I have the mug now.

extra.text: Do you know what a chairman does, Jensen?
Sits?
Sits higher. That's the job: a taller chair. I had one made, and it's on your stage now, waiting.
You put a chair on my stage?
A tasteful one, in mahogany, that swivels toward the money.
I'm renaming it, by the way. "Brisket" sounds edible.
It's supposed to sound like something you'd wait twelve hours for.
The Mahogany One. Doesn't that sound like it could buy a hotel?
It sounds like a dresser.
A dresser that could buy a hotel.

wrap.text: Eleven Directors, lost to a bus lane. I'll be raising this at the next meeting.
When's the next meeting?
Seven o'clock. Your stage. Bring the cone.

pause.text: Take your call. I'll wait. I'm very good at waiting for people to fold.

resume.text: Back? Was that a fan? How quaint. Where was I. Ah, yes: threatening you.

lines.text: Hi. Hi. Before you say anything, I know, I know, I know.
You sold my cone.
A guy in a suit offered me a thousand dollars and said he was a collector and he had a velvet bag, and collectors have velvet bags!
Wesley, it was a decoy. They swapped it. The real chip's somewhere else.
I know! I'm the worst fan, I'm a bad fan, and Chat is being so mean to me right now.
Hey. Hey. You're not a bad fan.
I'm not?
You're the only fan I've ever called back while eleven men chased me down a freeway.
Eleven?
They have quorum.
I'm gonna fix it. The suit guy who bought the cone, I've got him on stream, and I'm gonna find his car.
Wesley...
I'm gonna fix it so hard!

missions.title: Take Private
missions.stakes: Wesley found the grey SUV. The Board's having a meeting outside.
missions.passLine: Brisket is back. The stage is not.

steps.text: THE STACK
I found him! Grey SUV, off the stack, going north up the 87 to the rose garden in the river park, and Chat says it's a board meeting outside, which is called an offsite. I fixed it!

steps.name: the grey SUV
steps.objective: Tail the grey SUV to the Board's offsite.

lines.text: I'm watching the kid's stream, grey SUV going north up the 87, you on him?
I'm on him. Not too close.
Not too close is the whole art, boss. You tail a guy like you're dating his cousin, interested but not weird.
That's a terrible analogy.
Twenty years tailing guys and every analogy's terrible and they all work.
He's heading for the rose garden.
Course he is, that's an offsite guy, and in New York he held a board meeting in a rowboat and made the Directors row, and nobody steered.
Nobody steered?
That was the point. They went in circles for an hour and voted on it.
Nico. Why'd you really leave New York?
Honest? The kid with the laptop. Watching him get his name back... it made me want a new one.
A new name?
A new everything. Sun. Brisket. A boss who says please.
I say please.
You say "please welcome." It's different.
...Please welcome, to the Greenlight family: Nico. Driver. Pothole namer. Out-of-eleven guy.
See, that's nice. That's a nine.
Out of eleven?
Don't push it.

extra.text: How's she handling?
Like a dream.
Whose dream?
Mine.
Your dreams got curbs in them, boss.
The Pope's coming up on your right, so hold on to something.
I'm holding the wheel.
Hold on to something spiritual.
You're doing my word.
It's a good word. It's going round. Lola says you're wearing it out.
Does the car have a name?
The kid called it "the car."
That's not a name.
He was going through a lot.
Here's what we do. A name, a little card, and a launch. Tonight, after the keynote, the car gets a keynote.
After tonight you can call her Brisket Two for all I care.

wrap.text: That's the garden. Park somewhere they'll ticket you, it's more dramatic.
Is that a real rule?
In New York it's the only rule.

tooClose.text: Back off, you're in his mirror like a bad tattoo.
Too close! He can read the label on your jacket!

lost.text: Where'd he go? Find him, boss, the meeting doesn't wait.
Lost him? Look for the guy who drives like he owns the road, then look for the road.

steps.objective: Break up the board meeting.

during.text: Motion to restrain!
Seconded!
Motion denied!
All in favour of hitting him?
Watch the jacket! The Board wants the jacket!
Nobody gets the jacket. The jacket has a call time.

steps.text: There you are. Warm, a little dusty, and you've had a very big day.
I'll hold it! I'll hold it like a baby bird!

steps.label: BRISKET HEAT
steps.why: Brisket overheated in Wesley's hands. It still works, but it's very upset.

lines.text: It's getting warm. It's getting so warm. Is it supposed to be this warm?
Hold it level, Wesley. Like a cake. Like a very expensive cake.
It's beeping! Does it beep? Chat says it's never beeped before!
Lola's cooler. We need Lola's cooler. Don't let go.

steps.name: the Board's Directors
steps.objective: Get Brisket to Lola's cooler.

during.text: There's four black cars behind us and they're all signalling. Who signals in a chase?

steps.text: Give it here. Cooler. Blue one. That costs extra, and so does the ice.
I'm going back to the line. Pruitt's been lying there since four.
Congratulations on the chip. I don't need it any more. I have your stage, your screen and your stage manager's headset. See you at seven. Regards, the Board.

lines.text: They took my headset.
Marge?
Eleven men in suits walked into my building and took my headset off my head. Nobody touches the headset, Jensen. NOBODY.
Are you okay?
I'm on the loading dock next to a mop. They locked the stage doors, and the Board is in your green room eating our board's fruit.
Marge. I've got Brisket.
...You do?
It's in Lola's cooler, a little dusty, very happy to see me.
Okay. T-minus twenty-two. Doors are open, the fans are in, and our stage belongs to a man with a swivel chair.
How do I get in?
You don't get in. You get delivered. Lola's truck has a dock pass. Stay behind Lola.

missions.title: Fan Line
missions.stakes: Lola's truck has a dock pass. Stay behind Lola.
missions.passLine: Through the dock door, with a busboy in a jacket.

steps.text: THE MARKET SQUARE

steps.name: show
steps.label: DOORS
steps.why: Seven o'clock. Mr. Board walked out on your stage.

steps.name: Lola's truck
steps.objective: Stay behind Lola's truck to the arena.

lines.text: Stay behind me. Don't pass me. Nobody passes the truck.
Copy.
Don't "copy" me. Am I Marge?
...Okay.
Better. At the dock I say "catering," and you say nothing, because you're a busboy.
Lola, I'm wearing the jacket. Everyone in the world knows the jacket.
So take it off.
Then you're a busboy in a jacket. It's San Jose. Who looks twice?
About March. I didn't forget I booked you.
You forgot.
I forgot. I'd book you again. Every March.
Every March costs extra.
Then I'll pay extra, and I'll sign the check "love."
I know you will. You sign everything "love." It's the one thing about you I'd never change.

wrap.text: Dock's blocked. Black cars. You shove, I yell.
What do you yell?
"Catering!" It opens every door in this city.

pause.text: Who's calling you in a convoy? Take it. Stay behind me.

resume.text: You done? Good. Still behind me? Good.

lines.text: Chat knows everything, and there's twenty thousand people in there, and like nine thousand of them watch me!
Nine thousand?
It's a lot of guys named Kyle. Here's the plan: when the Board walks out, nobody claps, not one clap, total silence.
Twenty thousand people, silent?
Chat's calling it "the quiet launch," and Pruitt's handing out signs that just say "no," lowercase, because it's more hurtful.
That's... honestly brilliant.
You think I'm brilliant?
I think you're a good fan, Wesley. I think you're a good... I think you're good.
Can I put that on a shirt?
You can put it on a shirt.
Chat! He said I can put it on a shirt!

steps.objective: Clear the dock.

people.sub: the loading dock, beside a mop

lines.line: You're late.
It's six fifty-one.
By my standards you're late. By anyone else's, you're a miracle. Don't tell anyone I said that.
I brought sixty brisket plates and a CEO. Where do you want them?
Plates to the green room. CEO to the stage, through about eleven men.
Wait! Wait wait wait! Don't hit me! I'm pivoting!
Which way?
Your way! He gave me the lobby, Jensen, the real lobby, a table by the coat check with a sign that says "also."
"Also."
"Also: Cobalt." Under a ficus. I've never been so humiliated by a plant.
You want to help? Grab a tray.
I'll take the side door. My interns are loyal and emotionally unavailable, which is... it's actually perfect.
Dex. Thank you.
Don't thank me. Mention me, in the keynote, once. Like, "Dex: present."
Walkie. Channel two. You walk out at seven, not seven-oh-one, not seven-nineteen.
Seven. Copy. And Marge, I'll get your headset back.
You'd better. I can't call a cue into a mop.
You could. It would be a very short show.

steps.objective: Hold the dock door.

during.text: Interns! Synergy! Go!
Not my trays! Hit him, not my trays!
Five minutes! Jensen! Five!
Point of order!
Order denied!

missions.title: Showtime
missions.stakes: Seven o'clock. The Board walks out first unless you do.
missions.passLine: Seven-oh-four. The earliest keynote in Greenlight history.

steps.text: THE ARENA · BACKSTAGE

steps.name: curtain
steps.label: CURTAIN
steps.why: Seven o'clock. The Board walked out first.

steps.objective: Sneak across the back lot to the stage door.

during.text: Channel two. Three suits on the lot. The one with my headset is by the barrier. Go left of the trucks.
Quiet. They hear leather.

steps.objective: Get Marge's headset back.

during.text: Motion to keep the headset!
Seconded!
Motion denied, and that one's personal.

steps.text: I can hear my headset breathing. Bring it to the wings. Standby, sunrise.

lines.line: Good evening. I'm the Board. I'll be your Jensen tonight. Please hold your applause.
Nobody clap. Nobody clap.
...Thank you for holding it. Forever, apparently.
Chat, he's sweating. He's sweating on a ninety-metre screen.

slide.title: THE MAHOGANY ONE
lines: On a velvet stand of anticipation

lines.line: Tonight, a chip so fast it finishes your sentences: the Mahogany One, formerly Brisket, which sounded edible. It's on a velvet stand of anticipation.
It is edible. Spiritually.
Jensen. You're not on the run of show.
He is now. I just wrote him in.
You brought it. How thoughtful. Hand it here, and I'll thank you by name.
Ladies and gentlemen. Brisket.
NOW clap! NOW!
That's my keynote.
It's a lovely keynote. You have a lovely chair.
It swivels.
Toward the money. I heard.

steps.prompt: The room is yours. Open with...

options.reply: First, a thank-you to the jacket, which has been on time to every keynote for twenty years. Unlike me.
Somebody here slept in a tent since Tuesday, and somebody slept in a smaller tent inside his tent. This one's for you.
Let me show you something. Ninety-one percent of you are standing, which is the fastest standing ever measured indoors.

lines.line: They booed me in a parking lot. I only wanted one room to stand up.
Then sit in one first. That's the only way it works.
Let me tell you the real story. Booth three, coffee, a napkin, a pen you had to blow on, and no dog.
There was a dog! He followed you from my truck!
...There was a dog.
I drew one square on that napkin. Thirty years, people ask what was in it.
What was in it?
Nothing. It was a room. I just didn't know who'd be in it yet.
Is this the part where I lose?
This is the part where you sign something. You love a signature, and so do I.

options.reply: Wesley's cone. You paid a thousand dollars for it. Sign it 'sorry,' and he'll sell it for two.
Your resignation from my board. Point four percent. Sign it 'love,' it's legally a greeting card.

lines.line: ...Regards.
Close enough.
This isn't over, Jensen. I'm still on the board of a mattress company.
Get some rest.
Dex! Present!
Ladies and gentlemen: Dex. Present.
He said it on the big screen! Pivot! No, no pivot, I'm staying right here!
Seven-oh-four.
Is that bad?
It's four minutes late. ...It's the earliest we've ever been.
Front row. Sit. Watch one from the seats. I'll call my own cues: sunrise, walk, chip.
Standby, sunrise.
Sixty brisket plates in the lobby, first come.
Lola. The more you buy...
...the more you save. Fine. Just tonight.
Can you... would you... just once more?
Give me the phone. "To Wesley, my favourite fan. Love, Jensen." Right on the screen. You'll never read a text again.

options.reply: Ladies and gentlemen, the Greenlight Kestrel. We made exactly one. It's warm, it's right here, and you can't have it.
The Greenlight Kestrel. And remember, the more you buy... we only made one, so nobody's saving anything tonight.

steps.text: Chat says that's the loudest room in San Jose history. Chat's crying. Kyle's crying.
Chat says that was a solid nine. Out of eleven. Nico's going to be so proud.

people.sub: by the white car, the arena dock

lines.line: Boss. The car's parked and nobody touched her, and the whole day, start to finish? Eleven out of eleven.
I thought nobody gets an eleven.
Nobody did. Till today.
We're naming the car tomorrow. There'll be a keynote.

steps.title: THE MORE YOU BUY
story: Seven-oh-four. The earliest keynote in Greenlight history.

steps.text: Big fan. Still. Regards, the Former Board.
P.S. The mattress company would like a keynote.
